subject: Using posterior mean range for correlation plots

messages.author: f09a4f9db82a4609
messages.subject: Using posterior mean range for correlation plots
parts:
Hi,

I would like to visualise the autocorrelation of a dependent variable without considering any fixed covariates. This might seem strange to some, but it is relevant for my research. I am less certain about the next part though. Since there is little prior information to go on, I would build a model with an intercept and a barrier SGF based on an acceptable diffuse prior for range. Then I would use the approach described here, but using posterior mean range instead of a prior range to calculate the precision matrix for visualising the spatial autocorrelation. I have not yet found any clear arguments against this approach myself, but as I am quite new to INLA and the Bayesian framework I would be grateful to get some feedback if I am making a mistake.

Thank you for your time,
Sam

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Using posterior mean range for correlation plots
parts:
The approach described in Haakon's notes, are for looking at properties
for the prior. From what you write, it seems that you're interested in
the properties of the posterior, which is somewhat different. You could
consider to estimate what you want from 'inla.posterior.sample' maybe
using the 'inla.posterior.sample.eval' help you out. Then you would use
the samples to estimate empirically the correlations between the SGF.

Best
H
